## Closed-door deposition (February 28, 2024)

On Wednesday, February 28, 2024, Hunter Biden testified before two GOP-led House committees conducting the [[biden-impeachment-inquiry|impeachment inquiry]] into President [[joe-biden|Joe Biden]], telling lawmakers in a closed-door deposition that his father was not involved in his various business deals.[n] In a prepared opening statement he contested the premise of the inquiry, saying he "did not involve my father in my business" and that his testimony "should put an end to this baseless and destructive political charade."[n] He accused the committees of having "hunted me in your partisan political pursuit of my dad" for more than a year, trafficking in "innuendo, distortion, and sensationalism" while ignoring clear and convincing evidence, and asserted that there was no evidence for what he called "MAGA-motivated conspiracies" about his father.[n]

Republicans on the [[house-oversight-committee|House Oversight]] and [[house-judiciary-committee|Judiciary]] Committees had long sought his testimony, moving in January 2024 toward holding him in contempt of Congress before he agreed to appear voluntarily; they argued the testimony was a "critical component" of an inquiry centered on allegations that the president profited from his family's foreign business dealings while vice president.[n] Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] noted that Hunter Biden clips ran in "marathon mode" on social media that day, with legislator soundbites and screen grabs from [[marco-polo|Marco Polo]]'s Biden Laptop Report going viral again.[n]

Separately, the trial of former FBI informant [[alexander-smirnov|Alexander Smirnov]] — charged with feeding agents false claims that [[burisma|Burisma]] executives had paid Hunter and his father $5 million each — was set for April 23, 2024.[n]

## February 2024 annual physical

While his son [[hunter-biden|Hunter Biden]] was being deposed by House Republicans on February 28, 2024, President Biden underwent his annual physical.[n] According to the White House doctor's report, "The President feels well, and this year's physical identified no new concerns. He continues to be fit for duty and fully executes all of his responsibilities without any exemptions or accommodations."[n] The report disclosed that Biden had been placed on PAP therapy for sleep apnea and takes six medications for atrial fibrillation, cholesterol, reflux and seasonal allergies, and included a lengthy section on his gait and feet along with confirmation of sensory peripheral neuropathy in his feet.[n] Asked how the physical had gone, Biden said, "everything's squared away. There's nothing different from last year… everything's great."[n]

Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] mocked the neuropathy finding as "doctor speak for a stumbly wumbly diagnosis" and questioned whether Biden would be competent enough to stand trial for high crimes and misdemeanors in the [[us-senate|Senate]], given that Special Counsel [[robert-hur|Robert Hur]] had effectively concluded he was not competent to stand trial for lesser offenses.[n]

## Adam Rubenstein's account of newsroom bias (2024)

In February 2024, former opinion editor [[adam-rubenstein|Adam Rubenstein]] published a lengthy essay in [[the-atlantic|The Atlantic]] describing what he characterized as pervasive bias and activism at the paper, following similar accounts by former Times figures ranging from [[bari-weiss|Bari Weiss]] to his former colleague [[james-bennet|James Bennet]].[n] Rubenstein described a newsroom in which his passing remark about liking Chick-fil-A drew condemnation from shocked colleagues, and in which staff routinely rejected conservative viewpoints, imposed added demands and editing on conservative contributors, and resisted working on such pieces.[n]

Rubenstein had been involved in the 2020 controversy over the paper's publication of Senator [[tom-cotton|Tom Cotton]]'s op-ed arguing for possible use of the National Guard against violent rioting around the White House — an episode [[jonathan-turley|Jonathan Turley]] called one of the lowest points in the history of modern American journalism, noting that Times reporters denounced the column as inaccurate and inciteful and claimed it endangered them, while the paper a year later published a column by an academic who had suggested there was nothing wrong with murdering conservatives and Republicans.[n] Rubenstein observed that on January 6, 2021 few at the paper remarked that liberals were cheering the National Guard deployment against rioting at the Capitol — precisely what Cotton had urged.[n]

## Immigration tops the "most important problem" list (February 2024)

A Gallup survey conducted February 1–20, 2024 found that significantly more Americans named immigration as the most important problem facing the United States (28%) than a month earlier (20%), pushing it past "the government" — which had ranked first each month from January through November 2023 — for the top position.[n] In the same poll, 20% named the government, 12% the economy and 11% inflation; immigration was the only issue showing meaningful month-over-month change.[n] Gallup, which began compiling mentions of immigration in 1981, noted that the 28% reading essentially tied the record 27% from July 2019, and that immigration had previously ranked first five years earlier during a surge of attempted border crossings by Central American migrants, as well as in July and November 2018 and July 2014.[n]

## February 2024 zero-balance glitch

On Wednesday, February 28, 2024, Coinbase suffered a glitch that caused many users to see a balance of zero when opening their accounts.[n] "We are aware that some users may see a zero balance across their Coinbase accounts and may experience errors in buying or selling," the company said in a statement, adding that its team was investigating and that "your assets are safe."[n] Coinbase later posted on X that it was "beginning to see improvements in customer trading," though increased traffic meant some customers might still see errors in login, sends, receives and certain payment methods.[n]

The outage coincided with a sharp move in [[bitcoin|Bitcoin]], which had just spiked to its highest level since November 2021 before losing about $2,800, or over 4%, within minutes shortly after noon Eastern as reports of the outage spread on X.[n] Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] described opening the app to a $0 total herself and expressed skepticism at the official explanation, questioning whether traders would really have dumped BTC within minutes of learning of a glitch during a rally, and concluding: "to be on the safe side, maybe avoid Coinbase."[n]
